issue_ledger.exact_blocker: Automated bootstrap treats only three files as non-self-amendable ROOT_BOOTSTRAP_PATHS, while its allowlist permits broad scripts/, .github/workflows/ and requirements-validation.lock changes. The admission-authority contract names additional privileged reconciler, validator and authoritative status-writer executables. A candidate can preserve checked declarative invariants while modifying another privileged executable that becomes trusted after merge, yielding one-step-delayed authority self-amendment.
issue_ledger.next_action: Do not treat the installed three-file bootstrap root as a transitively closed authority TCB. BIL00 should close the trusted root before any future automated authority rotation relies on it.
issue_ledger.next_test: Using accepted-main bootstrap code, mutate reconcile_open_prs.py to unconditional context success, mutate one trusted validator to unconditional PASS, weaken one authoritative status-writing workflow, and alter requirements-validation.lock while preserving declarative JSON invariants; each candidate must be rejected solely because a root-TCB path changed.
issue_ledger.proposed_v25_fix_or_falsifier: Mechanically derive a non-self-amendable bootstrap root from config/admission_authority.json plus its runtime dependency lock: bootstrap policy/workflow/reconciler, normal trusted reconciler, every trusted validator entrypoint, every authoritative status-writing workflow, and requirements-validation.lock. Any change to that transitive set requires a separate independently trusted root-rotation/seed path.

issue_ledger.exact_blocker: The read-only diagnostic job checks github.event.pull_request.head.sha, but the privileged trusted-bootstrap job forwards only PR_NUMBER and CANDIDATE_DIAGNOSTICS_RESULT. The verifier then refetches the PR and uses its current head SHA, while cancel-in-progress is false. Diagnostics success for head A can therefore be consumed after the PR advances so that later head B receives the bootstrap decision without an equality proof tying B to the diagnosed bytes.
issue_ledger.next_action: Bind diagnostics and privileged bootstrap to one immutable candidate/base tuple before any future authority-changing PR is trusted.
issue_ledger.next_test: Add a synchronized A-to-B PR-head race fixture: diagnostics succeeds for A, PR advances to B before privileged reconciliation, and B must receive no successful bootstrap status from A's diagnostic result.
issue_ledger.proposed_v25_fix_or_falsifier: Pass DIAGNOSED_HEAD_SHA and DIAGNOSED_BASE_SHA from the pull_request_target event into the privileged job and require exact equality with the API-refetched PR head/base before any status publication; fail closed on mismatch.

issue_ledger.exact_blocker: trusted_bootstrap_success() accepts bootstrap authority by commit-status context text, success state and creator.login == github-actions[bot]. Multiple workflows share that principal; the predicate does not establish that the status came from the designated immutable bootstrap workflow/run on the exact diagnosed head/base. This is weaker than the authority contract's claimed source-verified bootstrap semantics.
issue_ledger.next_action: BIL00/EXT01 should bind bootstrap approval to a mechanically distinguished workflow/run or dedicated principal before depending on the context as authority provenance.
issue_ledger.next_test: Publish or fixture a successful supernova/bootstrap-admission status from a different workflow under the same github-actions[bot] principal; the trusted reconciler must reject it. Positive fixture must prove designated workflow identity plus exact head/base/event.
issue_ledger.proposed_v25_fix_or_falsifier: Require a completed successful run of the designated immutable authority-bootstrap workflow for the exact candidate head, expected base and allowed event via GitHub Actions run identity, or use a dedicated App/check source identity enforceable by the ruleset. Context+shared creator alone must not authorize authority drift.

issue_ledger.exact_blocker: The critical transition regression test verifies expected-base enforcement by reading transition_guard.py as text and asserting that three source substrings exist. It does not execute the guard. Dead code, an unreachable check, an altered call path or a refactor could preserve those strings while disabling the safety property, so the test is structurally vacuous with respect to behavior.
issue_ledger.next_action: Replace source-string presence assertions with executable behavior tests and freeze them before relying on the transition guard for a second clean countable cohort.
issue_ledger.next_test: Invoke the trusted guard against temporary Git repositories/roots covering exact-base PASS; missing expected_base_head on a state-changing transition FAIL; state/control/assignment mismatch FAIL; stale base FAIL; missing atomic companion path FAIL; and historical Gen6 non-transition/backward-compatible PASS.

Keep source-text assertions only as supplemental lint, not nonvacuity evidence.
